findings.title: Date override path returns true before busy-time checks
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot falls inside a date override the function sets dateOverrideExist and then returns true at line 133 before the busy.every(...) check at line 153. The busy array contains the host's Cal bookings and calendar busy times. As a result, any fixed host with a date override appears free for the whole override even when already booked, so personal and round-robin events can create double bookings on override days. The override should bypass normal working-hour checks only; busy times still need to be evaluated.

findings.title: Working-hours check mishandles days off and split shifts
findings.body: The new working-hours guard uses workingHours.find and returns false only when the first entry whose days includes slotStartTime.day() does not contain the slot. This has two failure modes: (1) if the user has no working-hours entry for that weekday, find returns undefined and the slot falls through as available, so fixed hosts can be booked on their days off; (2) if the user has multiple ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, an afternoon slot is compared only against the first range and rejected even though it is within the second range. In addition, line 142 sets end equal to start instead of using slotEndTime, so a slot that starts before closing but ends after closing is not rejected. The check needs to reject missing weekday entries and test the slot against all matching ranges, including the slot end.

findings.title: Date override interval only rejects slots wholly before or after it
findings.body: The containment test rejects a slot only when slotEndTime is before/equal overrideStart or slotStartTime is after overrideEnd. It therefore accepts slots that partially overlap an override: a 13:30-14:30 slot with a 14:00-18:00 override starts before the override but ends inside and is treated as within the override; a slot starting exactly at 18:00 is also accepted because the end check uses strict isAfter. Combined with the early return on dateOverrideExist, these slots bypass normal working hours and busy checks. The condition should require slotStartTime >= overrideStart and slotEndTime <= overrideEnd. Separately, the zero-length override check at line 114 compares two Dayjs objects with ===, so a start-equals-end override is never recognized as the unavailable case.

findings.title: Active date overrides are still selected by the override wall-clock UTC date
findings.body: activeOverrides is selected by comparing dayjs.utc(override.start) directly against the invitee's local day boundaries. Date override start values are stored as wall-clock times (for example, 14:00 Asia/Kolkata is stored as 14:00Z), so this comparison works only when the organizer and invitee dates happen to align. For a large positive invitee offset such as UTC+14, an override stored at 14:00Z on the invitee day falls after the invitee day's UTC end boundary (10:00Z the same day), so the override is filtered out and the new timezone conversion is never applied. The filter should compare the converted instant or otherwise test overlap against the invitee day.

findings.title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin date override fix
findings.body: The PR description says fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events are fixed and should prevent bookings when the fixed host is unavailable, but the added test only changes the invitee timezone for a personal event. It has no ROUND_ROBIN event, no fixed host with a date override, and no busy booking on the override day. As a result, the regressions in checkIfIsAvailable (busy times being skipped and the working-hours filtering) are not caught. Add a scenario with a round-robin event, a fixed host whose date override restricts availability, a loose host, and an existing booking during the override.
